title: Mixed-dtype runtime decision graph with sample-based calibration checks
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Implement a runtime decision graph that chooses execution dtype paths (FP16 / FP8 / INT8 variants) per-request and per-layer using quantization profiles and an integrated sample-based calibration/accuracy validator. The goal is to reduce token cost while keeping generation quality within SLOs for customer-facing models. The dispatcher must support shadow validation runs, per-layer gating based on calibration statistics, and automatic safe fallbacks to higher-precision paths when accuracy risk is detected.
acceptance_criteria: Dispatcher can select a dtype path at request time using model's quantization profile and per-layer thresholds
Shadow-run pipeline exists that executes a small fraction of requests on an alternate dtype path and publishes accuracy deltas to telemetry
Dispatcher triggers automatic fallback to FP16 for requests/segments that exceed configured accuracy/risk thresholds
End-to-end performance and cost tests demonstrate >=15% token cost reduction on targeted workloads without >1% regression in key ROUGE/BLEU/LM loss metrics
Console metrics surface per-route per-dtype success/failure rates and calibration drift alerts
design_notes: We propose a decision-graph abstraction rather than a simple heuristic chain. Nodes are: ProfileLookup, LayerConstraintResolver, ShadowSampler, ConfidenceGate, KernelSelector, FallbackHandler. ProfileLookup reads model-specific quant profiles produced by calibration jobs and annotates per-layer preferred dtype and quant parameters. LayerConstraintResolver enforces compatibility constraints (e.g. attention softmax numeric stability, layernorm scale factors). ShadowSampler marks ~1% of inference requests for parallel shadow execution on alternative dtype paths (configurable per-route). ConfidenceGate uses short-run token-level scoring (loss delta or KL proxy) for early detection within the first N tokens. KernelSelector maps chosen dtype/layer to a kernel bundle (vendor kernel + fallback CPU path). FallbackHandler implements graceful swap: finish current token on chosen path, then switch to higher precision for next step if needed, and emits a trace event for post-hoc verification.
implementation_plan: Schema: extend model manifest to include 'quant_profiles' with per-layer scale/zero-point and stability flags
Runtime: implement DecisionGraph engine with pluggable node adapter interface
Telemetry: add shadow-run labels and accuracy delta metrics to trace schema
Calibration infra: add lightweight post-deploy calibration job that periodically refreshes per-route profiles
Kernel mapping: maintain a kernel catalog that includes empiric latency/accuracy scores for each dtype per layer archetype
Safety: implement confidence gating heuristics (token loss delta, perplexity jump) and a safe-mode circuit breaker that forces FP16 when system latency/backpressure is high
API: expose per-route toggles in Console to enable/disable shadow runs, set sampling rate, and threshold values
test_plan: Unit tests for DecisionGraph node adapters
Integration test: run small model with synthetic inputs and assert shadow-run produces telemetry events
A/B perf tests: compare cost and latency with and without mixed-dtype dispatch on representative routes
Regression test suite: run PR candidate through calibration-driven shadow validation harness and verify no accuracy regressions beyond tolerance
Chaos test: simulate kernel failure to validate fallback handler correctness and no-request corruption
rollout_notes: Start with internal staging models and low-volume customer beta routes
Enable shadow sampling at 5% for first two weeks, monitor accuracy deltas and CPU/GPU overhead
If drift detected, pause sampling and escalate to on-call inference team
After stable signal, incrementally enable active dispatch on low-risk routes (non-critical latency-sensitive), then expand
